correctness.rationale: For k>=2, integer 1<=a<b, ak<n<bk, the cyclic ordered lifts satisfy all differences in [a,b]; coordinatewise minima preserve the periodic constraints. If positive deficits cannot be decremented, an active-index dependency cycle exists. A two-cycle across a gap would impose both a and b; a full cyclic chain would force all gaps to equal a or all b and n=ak or bk, excluded. Thus monotone descent to the meet, reversed descent from the target, realizes precisely the L1 cost for each lifted ordered matching. Cyclic order cannot be exchanged by unit legal slides, giving the lower bound and exact distance after minimizing lifts; frozen boundary cases correctly excluded. A separately coded exhaustive small case with 16 states and 256 pair distances found no discrepancy. Partial finite enumeration cannot prove universal isometry.
